correctness.rationale: The claim reduces exactly to a one-variable derivative sign after the odds substitution. For \(P_q=[1+(u+v)^q+(uv)^q]/[(1+u)^q(1+v)^q]\) and \(r=q-1\), the derivative sign is \(\Phi_r-1\) with \(\Phi_r=(1-u)(u+v)^r+u(uv)^r\). Convexity in \(r\), \(\Phi_0=1\), \(\Phi_1\le1\), and weighted AM–GM giving \(\Phi'_0\le0\) prove the needed signs for every \(-1<r\le1\). Entropy sign conventions, zero-parameter boundaries, the Shannon endpoint, and the published \(q>2\) obstruction were separately checked. The embedded deterministic checker reproduces the algebra numerically but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete finite-dimensional classification for the first genuinely nontrivial case of a published probability/information-theory conjecture. It identifies the conjectured endpoint \(q=2\) as exactly sharp for two summands and explains the full order interval by one structural convexity argument. This is more than a numerical instance or a routine substitution because it closes a continuous parameter range and separates monotonicity from the distinct concavity threshold.
